item.title: Salesforce CEO wants AI firms to follow this Hawaiian concept
item.description: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff urges AI firms to adopt kuleana, a Hawaiian concept of responsibility. He believes companies must proactively address potential AI risks before harm occurs. Benioff previously made a significant healthcare donation to Hawaii hospitals. This donation was the largest healthcare contribution in the state's history. He suggests product liability laws could hold companies accountable for AI harms.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: 'Unscheduled filming': Ganguly's biopic shoot leads to over Rs 6 lakh fine
item.description: Leicestershire have been fined £5,000 and deducted 27 points after their Grace Road pitch was deemed poor during the Glamorgan match. The club cited extreme heat and an unscheduled Bollywood shoot linked to Sourav Ganguly’s biopic as factors. However, the disciplinary panel rejected the filming as a mitigating factor, leaving Leicestershire facing a serious relegation battle.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER

item.title: Fortis moves Supreme Court against Delhi High Court order
item.description: Fortis Healthcare has appealed to the Supreme Court against a recent Delhi High Court order. The order mandated a forensic audit of Fortis's dealings with IHH Healthcare and RHT Health Trust. This legal battle stems from Daiichi Sankyo's efforts to enforce an arbitral award against former promoters. Fortis argues the high court order unfairly impacts its public shareholders and IHH.
item.dc:creator: RUPALI MUKHERJEE

item.title: ‘No basis in international law’: China rejects US tariff threat over Russian oil
item.description: China firmly rebuffs American attempts to influence nations purchasing Russian energy commodities. The US legislative proposal introduces tariffs on significant buyers of Russian oil and gas. Beijing denounces sanctions that lack a foundation in international law or UN backing. For its part, India emphasizes energy security and stays vigilant regarding US legislative actions, ready to implement measures to safeguard its trade interests.
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: US committed war crimes in 2 deadly strikes on Iranian school, sports centre: UN
item.description: An investigation by a UN mission revealed that US military operations on a school and sports facility in February were war crimes, resulting in the deaths of more than 150 individuals, including innocent schoolchildren. Additionally, Iranian authorities faced accusations of committing crimes against humanity during their protests, involving unlawful killings and torture of civilians, with findings set to be presented to the UN Human Rights Council.
item.dc:creator: PRANJAL PANDEY

item.title: Nicolas Cage bought Rhode Island estate for $15.7m, later sold it for $6.2m
item.description: Actor Nicolas Cage bought Rhode Island’s Gray Craig estate for $15.7 million in 2007 and listed it for $15.9 million a year later. The 27-acre property has a 24,000-square-foot stone mansion with 12 bedrooms, 10 bathrooms, ocean views, a tennis court, gym and pool. Cage eventually sold the estate for $6.2 million in 2011 to Massachusetts couple Andrew and Pamela Constantine.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Three African wild dogs travelled 4,126km in longest recorded mammal dispersal
item.description: A trio of African wild dog brothers undertook a remarkable odyssey covering 4,126 kilometers across Zambia. This unprecedented trek marks the longest documented dispersal by a mammal in Africa. Their journey through various terrains, including natural reserves and areas impacted by humans, highlights the crucial need for habitat connectivity beyond national park borders, revealing pressing conservation issues faced by species that require large ranges.
item.dc:creator: TOI SCIENCE DESK

item.title: Why Mark Zuckerberg's wife's school was shut down despite $125 million in donations,
item.description: Priscilla Chan's Primary School in East Palo Alto has shut down after ten years of operation. The school, backed by the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, faced challenges with academic performance. Funding from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative ceased, leading to the board's unanimous decision to close. While academic results were mixed, the school provided significant well-being and health support for students.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: 70-year-old hiker missing for a week on remote Michigan island rescued alive
item.description: After being missing for a week, 70-year-old hiker Craig Berg was miraculously found alive on Isle Royale on September 12. The search efforts proved critical, with fellow backpackers aiding in his discovery despite his injuries and hypothermia. Following his rescue, he was airlifted for urgent medical care, bringing an end to a challenging multi-agency search and rescue operation.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Meet Kishori Kudecha, 69, who started running at 60 and has 45 podium finishes
item.description: Kishori Kudecha took her first strides into running at sixty, reshaping her life and defying age stereotypes. Since then, she's accomplished impressive feats, including a full marathon and a 50 km ultramarathon, and accumulated more than forty-five podium finishes in various age divisions. Her ongoing commitment to fitness demonstrates that it is never too late to embrace a healthier lifestyle and serves as a motivation for many.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Bombs that wouldn’t explode, a bike that wouldn’t stay put: Rajasthan’s unique temples
item.description: Rajasthan's spiritual landscape features unique traditions beyond its royal history. Devotees worship rats at Karni Mata Temple and a motorcycle at Om Banna shrine. Tanot Mata Temple's faith intertwines with wartime stories and military protection. Mehandipur Balaji offers spiritual healing and protection from negative energies. Sanwariya Seth and Ramdevra showcase deities as business partners and cross-religious figures.
item.dc:creator: SHREEDHAR RATHI

item.title: Arman Tsarukyan picks Khabib vs Georges St-Pierre as dream UFC fight
item.description: Arman Tsarukyan proposed a dream UFC fight between retired champions. He wants to see Khabib Nurmagomedov face Georges St-Pierre in the Octagon. Both legendary fighters relied heavily on their elite wrestling skills. Their contrasting styles would create a fascinating tactical battle. Tsarukyan himself faces Mauricio Ruffy next in a significant bout.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Justin Gaethje ready for Ilia Topuria rematch after glove accusation
item.description: Justin Gaethje has welcomed a rematch with Ilia Topuria after their UFC bout. Topuria recently returned to social media and reignited their rivalry. Gaethje dismissed accusations regarding his gloves from their previous fight. He confidently pointed to his prior victory as a reason for accepting another match. The fighter also addressed critics and the glove controversy directly.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Delhi-NCR knew, so why didn't it act?
item.description: Delhi-NCR faces recurring incidents due to ignored warning signs and system failures. A traffic signal pole collapsed after warnings, and illegal constructions are being addressed. Road rage and hit-and-run cases highlight driver aggression and poor road discipline. Rising H1N1 cases and public transport disruptions strain the region's safety net. The region needs proactive prevention rather than reactive responses to ensure urban safety.
item.dc:creator: BIJU MATHEW

item.title: Watch: Messi wins 49th career trophy with 100th goal for Inter Miami
item.description: Lionel Messi scored his 100th goal for Inter Miami as they beat Cruz Azul 2-0 to win the Campeones Cup. The milestone came in his 115th appearance for the club, making him the fastest to reach 100 goals for any club or country. Messi, who has won 49 career trophies, is also preparing for his Argentina farewell.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER

item.title: America's Rorshach Test: Why Sydney Sweeney makes liberals go mad
item.description: That Sydney’s body had taken on deeper meaning beyond its corporeal form and become a political battleground was evident in 2022 when she threw her mother a 60th birthday party where one guest wore a Blue Lives Matter T-shirt and others wore red caps that said “Make Sixty Great Again”. That was enough for Sweeney to be cast out of the proverbial liberal heaven by some imaginary association with the Orange One.
item.dc:creator: NIRMALYA DUTTA

item.title: ‘Is this a joke?’: Being named Narendra Modi isn’t easy for these MP men
item.description: Five men in Madhya Pradesh share the highly recognizable name Narendra Modi, leading to amusing introductions and daily surprises. One retired principal often flashes his ID for confirmation, and a tea stall owner enjoys the curious inquiries of patrons. They navigate their lives with a unique connection to the prime minister's renowned identity.
item.dc:creator: KARISHMA KOTWAL

item.title: Accused was returning from club, cousin instigated him to chase woman biker
item.description: Two men were arrested for allegedly chasing and ramming a woman biker in Gurgaon. The accused were returning from a club when the incident occurred on Sunday. Police have described the event as a murder bid and formed a special investigation team. Investigators are recreating the alleged chase and examining footage from the incident. The two accused remain in police custody until Friday for further investigation.
item.dc:creator: NIKHIL SHARMA

item.title: Doctors away, driver 'takes over charge' in Kanpur hospital's OPD
item.description: A driver allegedly prescribed medicines to patients at a Kanpur government hospital. This incident occurred while the emergency medical officer was attending a court hearing. Hospital authorities have sought an explanation from the doctor regarding the driver's actions. The doctor acknowledged his driver wrote prescriptions and stated he removed him for acting independently. Action will be taken if the doctor fails to provide a satisfactory explanation.
item.dc:creator: FAIZ RAHMAN SIDDIQUI

item.title: NSE IPO opens today: Should you subscribe to the issue?
item.description: NSE is positioned to gain from increasing retail participation in the capital markets. However, its earnings continue to depend substantially on transaction volumes. NSE’s post-issue price-earnings (P/E) multiple of 42.9 is lower than BSE’s 53, even though NSE holds a dominant position in the market.
item.dc:creator: SMRITI JAIN

item.title: Football on table, wrestling without groundwork: Unusual sports India will play at Asiad
item.description: The Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games will introduce Indian spectators to a range of unique sports, such as teqball, kurash, soft tennis, sepak takraw, and sport climbing. These events not only highlight athletic prowess but also celebrate Asian culture. With a delegation of 503 athletes, India will participate robustly, showcasing diverse sporting talents on an international scale.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: Gold, silver price prediction: Will gold, silver continue to fall?
item.description: MCX Gold is likely to remain under pressure in the near term, with prices continuing to trade lower on a weekly basis and pointing to a sideways to bearish setup.
item.dc:creator: SMRITI JAIN

item.title: From torrential rain to typhoon threat: Asian Games face turbulent start
item.description: The Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya are at risk of disruption due to an impending tropical storm. Organisers are on high alert, as ongoing heavy rain has already led to the suspension and rescheduling of numerous events. In an unfortunate turn for China's cricket team, their campaign ended without any play taking place, all thanks to the relentless wet conditions.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: Video: US forces take out floating refuelling station allegedly tied to drug trade
item.description: US forces intercepted a floating refuelling station in the Eastern Pacific on September 16. This vessel allegedly supported illicit drug trafficking operations for Ecuador's Los Choneros organization. US forces removed the crew and transferred them to Ecuadorian authorities after clearing the vessel. The refuelling station was then sunk by US forces following the operation. This action aimed to disrupt logistical networks supporting drug trafficking in the Western Hemisphere.
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: A ‘Yash Thakur’ identity twist in Lucknow bonnet case
item.description: A woman was hit by a car and carried on its bonnet after an argument. She identified her attacker as Shahnawaz Ali, whom she knew as Yash Thakur. The confrontation began after she allegedly saw him with another woman in his vehicle. Police arrested Shahnawaz Ali and Danish, booking them under attempt-to-murder charges. The woman sustained injuries and lost consciousness after the incident.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Meet Sethuraman Panchanathan, first Indian-American named for top US engineering award
item.description: Sethuraman Panchanathan, an Indian American engineer and former NSF director, has been named the 2026 recipient of the National Academy of Engineering’s Arthur M. Bueche Award. He is the first Indian American and Arizonan to receive the honour, which recognises his work in science, technology policy, translational research and expanding opportunities nationwide.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Quote of the day by Sam Neill
item.description: Actor Sam Neill placed immense value on the importance of good co-stars, believing that enjoyable colleagues contribute significantly to a fulfilling work experience. This perspective underscores the idea that teamwork enhances not only productivity but also overall job satisfaction, transcending mere accolades. Neill’s own journey in acting stemmed from keen observation and hands-on experiences, a philosophy that resonates with aspiring professionals today.
item.dc:creator: TOI ENTERTAINMENT DESK

item.title: Man loses job weeks before becoming a father, finds an unexpected gift in it
item.description: After losing his job just weeks prior to becoming a father, Pratik Butani found an unexpected blessing in the time spent with his wife and newborn son. This period of reflection allowed him to dive into personal projects and cherish family moments, leading to profound lessons in perspective and gratitude. He now embraces this appreciation as he prepares for his next professional chapter.
item.dc:creator: TIMESOFINDIA.COM

item.title: Vishwakarma Puja: The day nobody touched the tools
item.description: At a bustling leather factory, Vishwakarma Puja was celebrated with Muslim workers paying tribute to the Hindu deity. Craftsmen paused their daily tasks to create stunning decorations, while a delicious biryani lunch from a local Park Street eatery added flavor to the festivities. Eschewing the customary Arandhan cooking restrictions of the day, this event beautifully illustrated the spirit of cultural unity among its participants.
item.dc:creator: PRASAD SANYAL

item.title: Pakistan cricket crisis deepens: Rizwan moves Lahore HC against cyber crime summons
item.description: Pakistan batter Mohammad Rizwan has moved the Lahore High Court against summons issued by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA). Rizwan, questioned after Pakistan’s Test series loss in England, has challenged the investigation and the agency’s jurisdiction. The case comes amid a separate PCB inquiry into player conduct and major squad changes following Pakistan’s poor England tour.
item.dc:creator: JYOTIRMOY HALDER

item.title: Ex-BJP MLA, dismissed cop booked for ‘gang-raping’ 22-year-old woman at knifepoint
item.description: An FIR was registered against former BJP MLA Narendra Pawar and Shailesh Patil. The duo allegedly gang-raped a 22-year-old woman at gunpoint on Thursday. The victim approached Pawar for help with a domestic dispute, which led to the incident. She was taken to a farmhouse and assaulted after being forced to consume alcohol. Police are investigating the case and Patil faces prior criminal charges.
item.dc:creator: PRADEEP GUPTA
